title: Localization over S commutes with tensoring over R
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $T\subseteq A$ a multiplicative subset, $M$ an $A$-module (an $R$-module via $R\to A$) and $T^{-1}M$ its localization, with $\ell:M\to T^{-1}M$, $m\mapsto m/1$. For an $R$-module $N$, the tensor product $M\otimes_RN$ is an $A$-module through $M$, and the $A$-linear map $\ell\otimes1_N:M\otimes_RN\to T^{-1}M\otimes_RN$ is a localization of $M\otimes_RN$ at $T$: it induces an isomorphism of $A$-modules $T^{-1}(M\otimes_RN)\xrightarrow{\sim}T^{-1}M\otimes_RN$, $(m\otimes n)/t\mapsto(m/t)\otimes n$. It is natural in $N$: for an $R$-linear map $f:N\to P$, the localization at $T$ of $1_M\otimes f:M\otimes_RN\to M\otimes_RP$ corresponds under these isomorphisms to $1_{T^{-1}M}\otimes f:T^{-1}M\otimes_RN\to T^{-1}M\otimes_RP$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization, line 2088: T^{-1}M = T^{-1}A (x)_A M) combined with Lemma Tag 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule, line 1881: T^{-1}A (x)_A (M (x)_R N) = (T^{-1}A (x)_A M) (x)_R N); used implicitly in the proof of Lemma 0523 (lemma-flat-module-powers, line 23827: 'it suffices to check that Tor_1^R(M,R/I) is zero on localization at q')
